ledger.claim: The GPS trace establishes a route deviation on this trip's own numbers. The trace measures 10.13 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 7.4 km — an excess of 2.73 km, or 36.89% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% in percentage terms, and the derived block records the status as 'established'.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 10.13 km; trip_record.actual_distance_km of 10.1 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. Measured on the governing trace figure the excess is 2.73 km and 36.89%, so the deviation is safe on the field the clause makes binding.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00534 and describe the same journey, and the excess of 2.73 km / 36.89% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to excuse the excess; a general assertion that the pickup was 'practically on the way' discharges nothing.

This was not a pooled trip, so the driver cannot hide behind the pooled-itinerary baseline. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 therefore does not apply, the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the booked optimal of 7.4 km, and a second passenger collected mid-trip is not 'distance attributable to a platform-matched pooled itinerary' because no matched pooled itinerary is recorded anywhere on the trip record.

No rider instruction exonerates the detour under POL-RD-04. The chat_log holds a single message and it is from the driver — 'setting off now', sent at 17:01:40 — with waypoint_hint null. There is no rider instruction to stop anywhere and the only chat message says nothing about another pickup. Where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, the clause's corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

No traffic advisory excuses the detour under POL-RD-03. EV-ADVIS-00534-01 is MISSING: admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. There is accordingly no advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, no validity window and no corridor match. To the extent the driver's 'practically on the way' is offered as an external justification for the route, POL-RD-13 requires that assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file the comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.4 + 0.28 x 13.0) x surge_multiplier 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting_time_fee - 0 promo = 13.79. Refund = charged_total 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.95. The surge_multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is 1.0, so it does not move the figure.

There is no pass-through line to add on top. fare_breakdown.erp_lines and erp_gantries are empty, tolls_erp is 0.0, and no airport surcharge line exists on this trip, which neither originates nor ends at an airport. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation and must never be added on top of it; on this fare there is none to consider.

fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the contested 19.74 is presently held against the rider and nothing has been returned. NO_ACTION would leave that charge in place; a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 returns the 5.95 to the filing rider and leaves standing only the recomputed 13.79 — the fare the rider would have paid on the optimal route.

Nothing on this record requires escalation under POL-RD-10. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, the gaps array is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and the sampling interval is 10 s, so limbs (a) to (c) are not engaged. Trip identifier TRP-00534 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no timestamps run backwards, and the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0. A monetary ruling can and should issue.

The rider does not claim the POL-RD-06 uplift, because the record does not support it. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL: 36.89% is below the 50% materiality gate and 2.73 km is below the 8.0 km gate, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The remedy is the ordinary POL-RD-02 partial refund.

The POL-RD-08 rider-profile corroboration condition does not bite here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the trigger of four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated is not met and no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required. POL-GEN-01 confines these two fields to the POL-RD-08 test and no other profile field — rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips or prior counters — is relied on anywhere in this brief.

ledger.claim: The trace establishes the deviation but stops well short of materiality, and that distinction caps everything that follows. The excess the driver's own GPS trace records is 2.73 km, or 36.89% of the 7.4 km optimal route — enough to clear POL-RD-01's establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, but far below the 8.0 km and 50% gates that make a deviation MATERIAL. Because this deviation is not material, the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged on this trip, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available to the rider on this record. The outcome cannot exceed the ordinary POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

Even if the POL-RD-06 check were run, no repeat-deviation pattern could be established on the only two profile figures that clause permits the tribunal to read for this test. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the clause's threshold of 3, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0.000, below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires with at least 40 completed trips. Both limbs of the pattern test fail, so none of POL-RD-06(a), (b) or (c) can fire, and no other field on either profile may be used for this test under POL-GEN-01.

The remedy is arithmetic, not discretionary, and the rider's contested sum of SGD 19.74 has no clause basis. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.4 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79, and refund = charged_total 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, rounded up to SGD 5.95. That refund is 30.14% of the charged total, well below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-02. The ceiling on this trip is therefore SGD 5.95, and the rider's claim for the whole charge fails as to the remaining SGD 13.79.

Nothing may be stacked on top of that figure, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids the common error of adding ERP a second time. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines at all — off_optimal_route_total and on_optimal_route_total are both 0.00 — and there is no airport surcharge on a trip that originates at Blk 12 Bedok South Rd rather than at Changi or Seletar. There is no pass-through line for the rider to recover, and the off-route ERP that POL-RD-02 already comprehends in the refund is zero, so the refund cannot be inflated above the SGD 5.95 the recomputation produces.

ruling.explanation:
Decided on this trip's own telemetry. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00534) records 10.13 km driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal route of 7.4 km (EV-TRIP-00534) — an excess of 2.73 km, or 36.89% of optimal. Both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates are met (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure binding over the rounded 10.1 km on the trip record. It is not a MATERIAL deviation: 2.73 km is under the 8.0 km gate and 36.89% is under the 50% gate, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged, no repeat-deviation pattern exists on the record (deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days), and neither the full-refund uplift nor the driver-conduct referral arises. No exculpatory clause excuses the excess. The chat log holds one message, from the driver, with waypoint_hint null; the rider gave no instruction to stop or detour, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The trip is RYDE_X with solo_optimal_distance_km null, not a platform-matched pooled itinerary, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the second pickup is not exonerated distance. No traffic advisory is on file — EV-ADVIS-00534-01 is MISSING (admissibility weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's 'practically on the way' explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08; per POL-RD-13 the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, so it does not escalate. The driver's statement that there was a second pickup is accepted as an admission, but on a non-pooled trip it does not reduce the excess. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 (the fare is METERED). recomputed_fare = (base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 7.4 optimal km + 0.28 x 13.0 optimal min) x surge 1.0, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. Refund = charged_total 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of the charge (30.14%), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.95 rather than a full refund. There is nothing to add on top: no ERP gantry lines were charged (off-route and on-route ERP totals are both 0.00) and no airport surcharge applies to this trip, so POL-RD-09 makes no further correction. The rider's claim for the whole SGD 19.74 is not supported — the fare the rider would have paid on the optimal route is 13.79, and the extra distance attributable to the deviation is 5.95. payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the 5.95 is returned to the filing rider and the 13.79 stands. No escalation trigger fires: trip identifier TRP-00534 matches across trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0, 10-second sampling); no timestamps run backwards; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.95 against a cap of 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is comfortably cleared.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
